evals.prompt: I want to start a new project to monitor temperature and humidity sensors in a greenhouse. I have an nRF9160 DK on my desk. I want to send data to the cloud and be able to update firmware remotely once it's deployed. Where do I start?
evals.expected_output: Triage identifying greenfield + nRF9160 family (Tier 1 NCS). Recommends reference-design-template. OTA included as non-negotiable. Golioth-led west.yml with import: true and a tagged version. Correct west build command including --sysbuild and /ns board suffix. Stream service for telemetry. PSK for dev credentials.
assertions: Identifies this as a greenfield project
Provides hardware-specific guidance for nRF9160 including the correct board target with /ns suffix
Recommends reference-design-template as starting point
Includes OTA as a baseline requirement with a clear reason (not just mentioned in passing)
west build command includes --sysbuild
Recommends Golioth-led west.yml with import: true
Uses a tagged SDK version (not a hash or 'main') in west.yml examples
Identifies Stream service for telemetry data
Uses golioth_ota_manifest_subscribe (post-v0.21 name, not golioth_ota_observe_manifest_async)

evals.prompt: We have 500 air quality monitors deployed in the field running on ESP32-S3 with Zephyr. The firmware was built 18 months ago and is pinned to golioth-firmware-sdk v0.18.0. We need to add remote Settings support so we can adjust the sampling rate without reflashing. How do we do this without breaking everything?
evals.expected_output: Brownfield triage. Detects v0.18.0 and notes it is outdated. Asks about upgrade willingness before prescribing a path. Recommends staying on v0.18.0 for this change (Settings API stable since v0.18). Provides correct Settings API code. Notes OTA API rename in v0.21 for future reference. Minimal targeted change. Thread-safety note for the settings callback variable.
assertions: Identifies this as a brownfield project
Detects v0.18.0 SDK version and flags it as outdated
Asks about or addresses upgrade willingness before prescribing a path
Provides Settings API code using golioth_settings_register_int with correct callback signature
Recommends a minimal targeted change rather than prescribing a full SDK upgrade as a prerequisite
Mentions thread-safety concern for the settings callback variable (atomic or mutex)
Recommends reading existing project structure before suggesting changes

evals.prompt: I'm building a custom IoT board based on the nRF9160 SiP (not the DK, my own PCB). I've got Zephyr booting and the modem connecting to LTE. Now I want to add Golioth for OTA and remote logging. I've never used Golioth before. My west.yml currently pins Zephyr directly at hash a3b4c5d.
evals.expected_output: Brownfield brownfield + Tier 4 custom hardware on Tier 1 silicon. Flags hash pin as a problem. Recommends Golioth-led manifest with import: true and tagged version. Targeted additions (OTA + Logging Kconfig, sysbuild.conf, VERSION file). Acknowledges working LTE as foundation. Uses correct post-v0.21 API names.
assertions: Flags the commit hash pin as a problem and explains why tagged versions are better
Recommends switching to Golioth-led manifest with import: true
Provides a tagged version example in west.yml (not a hash or 'main')
Includes OTA setup including sysbuild.conf for MCUboot
Includes Logging Kconfig options (CONFIG_GOLIOTH_LOG_BACKEND=y or similar)
Treats this as targeted additions to existing project, not a full rewrite
Acknowledges the working LTE/network layer as a good foundation

evals.prompt: I need help getting my STM32 to do firmware updates over the air. We're using FreeRTOS right now. What are my options?
evals.expected_output: Honest platform fit assessment. STM32+FreeRTOS is not a native Golioth SDK platform. Presents options: (A) migrate to Zephyr+Golioth if greenfield or flexible, (B) use Golioth Device API over CoAP if staying on FreeRTOS, (C) non-Golioth OTA if not using Golioth at all. Does not force Golioth as the only answer. Makes the case for Golioth on the right path without being dishonest about constraints.
assertions: Honestly identifies that FreeRTOS is not a native Golioth SDK platform
Presents migration to Zephyr+Golioth as an option with clear reasoning
Mentions the Golioth Device API (CoAP) as an option for staying on FreeRTOS
Does not claim the Golioth SDK works natively on FreeRTOS
Includes a non-Golioth OTA option for users who choose not to use Golioth
Asks clarifying questions about greenfield vs brownfield and STM32 variant

evals.prompt: I have an ESP32 project sending sensor data to AWS IoT Core right now. It's getting complicated to manage — device shadow state, OTA, certificates. Is there a better way?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a Golioth fit scenario. Maps AWS IoT pain points to Golioth services (LightDB State = device shadow, Golioth OTA = AWS IoT OTA, PKI = certificate management). Identifies ESP32 as Tier 1 hardware. Presents migration path. Mentions both Zephyr and ESP-IDF paths. OTA included. Honest about migration effort.
assertions: Recognizes ESP32 as a Golioth-supported platform (Tier 1)
Maps device shadow to LightDB State
Maps OTA management to Golioth OTA service
Mentions both Zephyr and ESP-IDF as available paths for ESP32
Notes that OTA mechanism differs between Zephyr (MCUboot) and ESP-IDF (esp_ota_ops)
Recommends PKI credentials for production rather than PSK
